entries.name: Correlated topic model
entries.definition: A mixed-membership topic model that draws each document's topic proportions from a logistic-normal distribution and generates its words through latent topic assignments and shared categorical topic-word distributions.
entries.identity_notes: Scoped to the Blei-Lafferty correlated topic model introduced at NIPS 2005 and developed in the 2007 journal article. The defining change is the logistic-normal document mixture, not a word-interaction MRF, dynamic topic evolution, sparse topic graph or the particular variational solver. Topic graphs are optional analyses of fitted latent coordinates. This is not the Dynamic Conditional Correlation econometric model. limitations: Fixed topic count, finite vocabulary and conditional bag-of-words assumptions remain. Flexible logistic-normal associations do not remove compositional constraints, identify unique semantic topics or establish that all Dirichlet laws are exact special cases.

The source assertion that one observed document leaves no advantage for a nondiagonal variational covariance is not a general theorem. Posterior dependence can remain. Substituting the auxiliary bound into an expected log probability, as displayed with equality in the appendices, must be read as a bound rather than an exact expectation.

The journal topic graph regresses standardized fitted logit means using lasso and combines neighborhoods. Gaussian precision statements concern specified Gaussian coordinates; graph estimates do not automatically establish conditional independence of proportions, gauge-invariant structure, causal links or consistency from noisy variational means.

Reported Science-corpus comparisons use importance sampling or partially observed-document prediction under particular fits. No universal performance or semantic-interpretability advantage is asserted. No author code or benchmark was executed.

claims.statement: For fixed K topics beta_k on a finite vocabulary, draw document logits eta_d from N(mu,Sigma), set theta_d=softmax(eta_d), then independently draw each topic assignment z_dn from theta_d and its word from beta_zdn, conditional on these variables. The logistic-normal prior allows associations that a single Dirichlet proportion prior cannot express, including positive pairwise proportion covariance when at least three components are available. Dirichlet proportions are not literally independent: their sum-to-one constraint gives negative off-diagonal covariance for positive concentration parameters. Common shifts of all logits leave proportions unchanged; unrestricted K-logit mean/covariance parameters are not uniquely identified by the induced composition. Logit covariance, proportion covariance and causal relationships are distinct.

claims.statement: The original inference scheme approximates each document posterior by independent univariate Gaussian logits and categorical topic assignments. An auxiliary positive scalar bounds expected log-sum-exp from above, yielding a tractable lower bound no greater than the exact mean-field evidence lower bound. Coordinate updates alternate the auxiliary scalar, assignment probabilities, Gaussian means and positive variances; variational EM fits topics and Gaussian parameters from approximate sufficient statistics. Nonconjugacy and the additional bound make this approximate inference, not exact posterior computation or a guarantee of global marginal-likelihood maximization. The journal correction restores entropy in the originally printed corpus bound; the inspected v2 reprint already includes it, and the corpus objective sums expected log joint plus entropy for each document.

entries.name: Dynamic topic model
entries.definition: A time-sliced topic-model family that links the softmax natural parameters of corresponding topic-word distributions across slices through Gaussian state transitions, allowing a fixed set of topics to change over time.
entries.identity_notes: Scoped to Blei and Lafferty's ICML 2006 dynamic topic models. Topic-word distributions evolve, unlike a static topic model with only changing document proportions. The full formulation also evolves the logistic-normal mean for document-topic proportions; the inference exposition explicitly simplifies that part to a fixed Dirichlet prior. Variational Kalman and wavelet approximations are fitting choices, not synonyms for the model family or neural state-space layers. limitations: The basic random-walk model fixes topic count and vocabulary and does not create or remove topics. Richer drift, heteroscedasticity and topic birth/death processes are proposed extensions. Time-slice choice and Gaussian innovation assumptions matter; temporal association is not a causal account of scientific change.

Softmax logits are invariant to a common shift. Fixed topic indexing links trajectories, while label permutation and model fitting can still limit semantic identification. The presented isotropic document-logit law does not itself fit the full static CTM covariance or evolving correlations.

Appendix A's displayed expected transition quadratic omits adjacent-time posterior covariance terms, and its entropy display does not give the joint correlated Gaussian entropy. A correct Gaussian-chain calculation uses cross-time covariance and the joint covariance determinant. With fixed surrogate variances some omitted terms are constant for mean optimization, but the printed expressions are not certified as exact complete objectives when variances change.

The reported next-year Science comparison uses a variational likelihood bound, as stated in Figure 5, rather than computed exact predictive likelihood. The illustrative wavelet approximation and historical results are not a universal accuracy or convergence guarantee. No author implementation or benchmark was executed.

claims.statement: For fixed topic count K and vocabulary, the basic model evolves each topic logit vector as beta_tk|beta_(t-1)k~N(beta_(t-1)k,sigma² I) and maps it through softmax to word probabilities. In the full generative description, alpha_t|alpha_(t-1)~N(alpha_(t-1),delta² I) evolves the document-topic logit mean. Each document draws eta~N(alpha_t,a² I), then topic assignments from softmax(eta) and words from the selected time-specific topic. Initial-state distributions and variance settings must be specified. Documents are grouped into ordered slices; conditional within-document word exchangeability remains. The inference example beginning on p.3 retains evolving topics but fixes a Dirichlet document-proportion prior, a stated simplification rather than an equivalent formula for the entire full model.

claims.statement: The published approximation uses Gaussian topic trajectories conditioned on optimized pseudo-observations, retaining time dependence within each topic chain while separating it from document-level latent factors. Expected topic-word counts connect document updates to trajectory fitting. Exact Kalman recursions for this Gaussian surrogate do not yield the exact nonconjugate multinomial posterior. The auxiliary expected-log-normalizer bound and numerical optimization introduce approximation; smoothing over a fitted interval can use later observations and must be distinguished from forecasting beyond that interval.

entries.name: Author-topic model
entries.definition: A generative document model in which each author has a shared topic-proportion distribution and each word is produced by uniformly selecting an author from the document's observed author set, selecting a topic from that author, and selecting a word from that topic.
entries.identity_notes: Scoped to Rosen-Zvi, Griffiths, Steyvers and Smyth's UAI 2004 author-topic model, whose arXiv deposit occurred in 2012. It conditions on a document's authors and pools topic preferences across their documents. It is distinct from document-specific LDA, a pure author-word mixture, author-recipient-topic models and personalized large language models. Latent token-author assignments are model variables, not observed intellectual contributions. limitations: Known author sets, uniform token-level author choice, fixed topic count, bag-of-words observations and stationary author preferences constrain the model. The author set is conditioned on, not generated. Coauthors with indistinguishable participation can be unidentifiable, and inferred assignments do not establish actual authorship contributions or expertise.

Topic and author probability vectors are conditionally independent given assignments under the conjugate construction, but their marginal posterior is generally coupled. The product of separate marginal posterior factors displayed in Equation (8) must not be taken as a general exact factorization. Reported prediction averages plug-in conditional means, which need not equal integrated multiword probabilities.

The historical held-out NIPS split ensures test authors already occur in training and can incorporate observed words from each test document. It does not demonstrate cold-start prediction for unseen authors. LDA overtakes the author-topic model in reported settings as more document words become available; no blanket superiority is asserted.

Symmetric-KL author similarity and topic entropy are descriptive applications. They do not validate reviewer selection, establish causal collaboration or supply calibrated measures of author competence. Finite Gibbs runs and restarts do not prove mixing, and no author software or benchmark was executed.

claims.statement: For fixed topic count T, draw each author topic vector theta_a from a symmetric Dirichlet(alpha) and each topic word vector phi_t from a symmetric Dirichlet(beta). Given a nonempty observed author set A_d, each token draws x uniformly from A_d, z from theta_x, and w from phi_z. Conditional on theta, the document-topic mixture is the arithmetic mean of its authors' topic vectors. Ordinary smoothed LDA is recovered when every document is assigned its own distinct single author and the priors match; sharing one author across documents instead pools their proportions. The author-word model requires deterministic unique topic assignment per author, a constrained degenerate case rather than a typical positive-Dirichlet draw.

evidence.locator: Sections 2.1-2.3, printed pp.488-489 / PDF pp.2-3, including smoothed-LDA footnote and special cases

claims.statement: The published Gibbs sampler jointly updates each token's author-topic pair after integrating theta and phi. For observed word v, eligible author a in A_d and topic t, the conditional weight is proportional to (n_vt^(-i)+beta)/(n_.t^(-i)+V*beta) times (n_at^(-i)+alpha)/(n_a.^(-i)+T*alpha). Counts exclude the current token; assignments outside A_d have zero weight. The uniform author-selection factor is constant among eligible pairs and cancels in normalization. Dirichlet posterior means conditional on sampled assignments estimate the author-topic and topic-word vectors; averaging across sampled assignments approximates marginal inference. Finite sampling and posterior-mean plug-ins are not exact multiword posterior predictive integration.

notes: All eight NIPS 2005 PDF pages visually read, including four figures, references and Appendix A. Title page authors Blei then Lafferty, unlike website metadata ordering. PDF has no visible numeric printed page labels; use PDF locators.

CTM replaces the document Dirichlet proportion prior by a logistic normal: eta~N(mu,Sigma), theta=softmax(eta), per-token topic z~Cat(theta), word~Cat(beta_z). K fixed. Word topic distributions are shared categorical probabilities. No direct within-topic MRF word interaction or temporal evolution is introduced.

Qualify the source rhetoric about LDA topic independence: Dirichlet components sum to one and have negative pairwise covariance, not literal independence. Logistic-normal flexibility can represent positive associations for K>=3; it does not mean every pair can be positively correlated or that CTM contains every Dirichlet distribution exactly.

K-dimensional softmax is nonminimal and invariant to common shifts. Equation3 gives log(theta_i/theta_K), which chooses a reference with eta_K=0; this is one representative, not a unique inverse for unrestricted K-dimensional Gaussian logits. Distribution of log-ratios, covariance of proportions and causal topic dependencies must be distinguished.

Mean-field q uses independent Gaussian logits and independent categorical assignments. Page4 assertion of no advantage from a nondiagonal covariance merely because fitting one document is not accepted as a theorem; richer variational families can improve bounds. Logistic normal is nonconjugate. The source adds an auxiliary tangent upper bound on expected log-sum-exp, so the optimized tractable bound can be lower than the exact mean-field ELBO. Equation10 uses equality when substituting that bound; do not treat it as exact expected log topic probability.

AppendixA gives zeta=sum exp(lambda+nu²/2), phi proportional beta_word*exp(lambda), iterative conjugate-gradient mean updates and positive-variance Newton updates. Model-parameter VEM uses expected Gaussian sufficient statistics and topic-word counts. These are approximate inference/estimation operations, not part of model identity or guaranteed exact likelihood ascent.

Science visualization uses 16351 OCR articles from1990-1999 with100topics. Separate predictive comparison uses1452documents from1960,5612words afterpruning,10foldCV and importance-sampled document probabilities proposed from fittedvariational distributions. Predictiveperplexityconditionsobservedsubset; no exact empirical likelihood or universal performance claim. Figure2 labels derived by turbo topics;graphnotcausal.

Corrected provisional Section 3 / Figure 2 references in the maintained record before formal review. Equation (17) exponent uses nu_i squared divided by 2 as expected.

One-page official correction fully visually read. It adds variational entropy H(q_d) to the corpus likelihood bound in the 2007 journal article p24. Proper corpus formula sums E_q log joint plus entropy for every document; the correction display leaves the entropy visually outside the summation and must be interpreted with matching per-document scope. This correction concerns the journal display; the NIPS2005 Eq4 already contains H(q).

All 20 pages of arXiv 0708.3601v2 visually read, including figures, Appendix and bibliography. Electronic reprint explicitly differs in pagination from journal pp.17-35; cite PDF/reprint page numbers, not offset-inferred journal numbers.

Core logistic-normal CTM and factorized variational approximation agree with the 2005 paper. Page 5 expressly notes the nonminimal softmax common-shift invariance. The rhetoric about Dirichlet independence is qualified by exact negative compositional covariance; page 6 acknowledges negative correlation.

The inspected v2 reprint page 9 already includes the entropy term in the corpus bound. The separately inspected correction concerns the originally printed journal p.24, not an omission in this inspected reprint. Entropy must be within the sum over documents.

Appendix page 17 Eq.12 supplies a valid tangent upper bound on expected log-sum-exp. Eq.13 displays equality when substituting that lower bound for expected log topic probability; interpret as a bound, not an exact expectation. Page 18 gives coordinate updates and only local optimization, not global or exact marginal likelihood guarantees. Nonconjugacy does not prohibit every conceivable Gibbs/MCMC scheme.

Pages 9-11 build optional sparse topic graphs by lasso regressions of standardized fitted variational means and AND/OR neighborhoods. Gaussian precision conditional independence is about specified Gaussian coordinates; estimated-logit graphs are not automatically proportion conditional-independence or causal graphs, especially under nonminimal softmax gauge changes. No generic consistency theorem for these estimated latent means is inferred from the cited observed-Gaussian regression theorem.

Pages 11-16 give Science OCR visualization and separate 1960 held-out prediction experiment, with importance-sampled probabilities and partially observed document perplexity. Code linked but not inspected/executed. Abstract says 57M words while page 11 says 5.7M; avoid adopting either count without resolution. Model comparison remains bounded to the reported settings.

Page 13 expected squared Hellinger expression uses sum of squared square-root differences (without conventional 1/2 normalization) and factorization across separately approximated documents; not a causal or human-semantic distance guarantee. Bibliography provides provisional leads, not inspected evidence for other concepts.
All eight pages visually read, including Appendix A, figures and bibliography. ICML 2006 author-hosted manuscript; no visible printed numeric page labels, so use PDF locators.

Section 2 defines time-sliced K-topic distributions using Gaussian random walks on softmax logits beta_tk, fixed K and vocabulary. The full generative description also evolves logistic-normal document-topic mean alpha_t by a Gaussian random walk. Document logits eta~N(alpha_t,a²I); tokens draw topics and categorical words. Isotropic innovations and fixed latent topic indexing do not model topic births/deaths, unequal time intervals, word-order syntax or causality.

Page 3 explicitly simplifies the inference exposition to evolving topic logits with a fixed Dirichlet document-proportion model. Do not attribute the full moving logistic-normal mean to every displayed update. Structured variational inference retains temporal Gaussian chains through optimized pseudo-observations, with topic chains separated from document latent factors.

Pages 3-4 describe variational Kalman filtering/smoothing and a wavelet-regression approximation. Exact forward/backward recursions concern the Gaussian surrogate; they are not exact posteriors for the nonconjugate multinomial observation model. Smoothing uses future observations within the fitting interval; it is distinct from forecasting on a future-held-out interval. Wavelet example is Haar, reported implementation uses Daubechies. No author implementation inspected or executed.

Appendix A page 8 requires qualification: the expansion of expected adjacent Gaussian differences omits adjacent-time covariance terms, despite a structured temporal q. Its displayed entropy sums marginal variances and even changes the sign of log variance; a correlated joint Gaussian entropy needs the joint covariance determinant. Fixed-variance omissions can be constants with respect to pseudo-observation means, but the printed expressions are not certified exact full objectives when variances change. The generic Jensen/ELBO identity and log-sum-exp tangent inequality remain valid.

Science experiment reports next-year comparisons at five-year increments, 20 topics and static baselines. Figure 5 caption explicitly uses a variational likelihood bound, not computed exact predictive likelihood. Corpus year/count descriptions vary (120 years, 1881-1999, 128-point wavelet illustration); record only bounded historical context, not universal gains or a replicated data specification.

Time-evolving topic-word laws distinguish DTM from static CTM, LDA and dynamic-document prevalence alone. Topic births/deaths and richer drift/heteroscedastic dynamics are suggested extensions, not properties of the evaluated fixed-K random-walk model.
All eight UAI 2004 pages visually read, printed pp.487-494 = PDF page +486, including all figures/tables and references. arXiv deposit is 2012, not publication date.

Each known author has a shared Dirichlet-distributed topic-proportion vector; each topic has a Dirichlet-distributed word-probability vector. Given nonempty observed author set a_d, each token independently selects one of those authors uniformly, then topic from that author, then word from topic. Marginal document-topic weights are the average over authors. Authorship metadata is conditioned on; no model generates the author set or determines actual intellectual contribution.

The p.489 LDA special case requires a distinct single author for each document (authors not shared across documents), with matching priors. One author shared by many documents pools their mixture and is not ordinary document-specific LDA. A pure author-word model requires deterministic unique topic per author, a degenerate constraint rather than an ordinary positive symmetric Dirichlet draw.

Page 490 Eq.4 jointly samples author and topic for each token after integrating theta and phi, using leave-one-token-out word-topic and author-topic counts. Author assignment is restricted to the observed set; uniform 1/|a_d| cancels in proportional weights only within that set. Dirichlet posterior means are conditional on assignments; averaging over samples approximates marginal inference. Finite sweeps/random restarts do not guarantee mixing or exact prediction.

Page 492 Eq.8 displays a product of separate marginal posteriors for theta and phi, but they are generally coupled after latent assignments are marginalized. Conditional on assignments they factorize. Reported evaluation uses posterior-mean plug-ins per assignment sample, averages samples and is an approximation, not exact integration of arbitrary multiword predictive probabilities.

Historical NIPS held-out set was chosen so every test author appears in training. Prediction after observing part of a test document updates distributions using those observed tokens. This does not establish cold-start authorship prediction or wholly unseen metadata. The paper reports LDA overtaking author-topic prediction as more words are seen; no blanket superiority is asserted.

Author similarity via symmetric KL and topic entropy are descriptive applications, not calibrated expertise, causal contributions or validated reviewer selection. Identical coauthor sets can make authors indistinguishable; uniform contribution and stationary author interests are assumptions. Topic label permutation and sparse author evidence limit identifiability.

native_neighbors.name: Latent Dirichlet allocation
native_neighbors.definition: A hierarchical model for collections of discrete observations in which each document draws a Dirichlet-distributed mixture over a fixed finite set of topics, and each token draws a topic and then an observation from that topic’s categorical distribution.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: The defining feature is a shared prior over document-specific topic proportions together with repeated per-token topic selection. This differs from PLSA’s fitted document-index weights and a mixture selecting one topic for a whole document. The model is distinct from its variational EM, sampling or other inference algorithms. The bare LDA alias is omitted because AIMech already uses it for the unrelated Gaussian classifier LinearDiscriminantAnalysis. The base fixed-topic-probability presentation and its Bayesian topic-prior extension are distinguished explicitly. Compared all 442 pinned AIO labels and scoped synonyms and 418 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. The initial normalized LDA hit denotes LinearDiscriminantAnalysis, whose full Gaussian-classifier record was read; the bare LDA alias is omitted from the new topic-model record. No normalized identity match remains for the final candidate names/aliases. Final full-checkout fixed-string searches, including ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main, return two lines each; both unique contents are existing frontier references. An additional broad LDA search returned 289 worktree and 237 main lines before the preceding batch merged; all 84 distinct contents were read, covering the existing classifier, topic-context references, unrelated programming mnemonics and namespace abbreviations. All 188 semantic label/synonym hits were read. Nineteen exact annotated AIO CLASS nodes and outgoing edges were inspected (18 verified unchanged from prior reading, Biclustering read here), along with their generated records and 16 native neighbors. The 35 contextual YAMLs were read or byte-verified after documented full reading. Absence is bounded to this snapshot, maintained corpus and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The number of topics is finite and fixed in this construction. Integrating a continuous Dirichlet mixture does not introduce infinitely many topic classes. Infinite exchangeability supports the representation discussed in Section 3.1; arbitrary finite exchangeability alone is not the asserted theorem.

Given observed topic assignments, Dirichlet conjugacy is exact. With topics unobserved, the marginal posterior over proportions is generally not a single Dirichlet; gamma=alpha+expected counts is a variational update, not exact marginal conjugacy. Exact inference is generally difficult, and bound optimization need not monotonically improve the true likelihood or attain its global maximum.

The basic model ignores word order and explicit within-topic dependencies, though integrating document proportions induces dependence between tokens. Zero word probabilities require smoothing or other support handling for novel documents. A prior over document mixtures does not guarantee freedom from overfitting, identifiable topics or meaningful semantic labels.

The Bayesian topic-prior extension requires expected log topic probabilities in its assignment update. The appendix’s printed alpha Hessian has a sign/factor mismatch with the preceding gradient; the consistent Hessian is M*(trigamma(sum alpha)-delta_ij*trigamma(alpha_i)). This record does not adopt that printed Hessian as verified code. Equation (13) correctly uses the normalized posterior.

The comparison’s empirical mixture over training-document indices must weight an entire document once; the printed p(d) inside its token product is not adopted. These mathematical qualifications do not establish an error in unseen author software or experiments.

The source’s document, classification and recommendation experiments have distinct protocols. No exact likelihood replication, generic performance advantage or biological-mechanism conclusion is claimed. All source material concerns the specified 2003 model, not every later topic-model extension.

claims.statement: For a fixed K, positive alpha_i and normalized topic-word probability rows B_i, draw theta_d~Dirichlet(alpha) independently for each document. Given a document length N_d, draw z_dn~Categorical(theta_d) and w_dn~Categorical(B_zdn) for each token. Conditional on theta_d and B, token probabilities are sum_i theta_di*B_iw and tokens are independent; integrating theta_d gives p(w_d|alpha,B)=integral Dir(theta_d;alpha)*product_n(sum_i theta_di*B_i,w_dn)dtheta_d. This is an exchangeable document distribution, generally with dependent tokens after integration. An unordered count vector additionally includes its multinomial multiplicity. The paper’s Poisson length law is optional to this conditional construction. For fixed B, its mean-field approximation is q(theta,z)=Dir(theta;gamma)*product_n Cat(z_n;phi_n), with phi_ni proportional B_i,w_n*exp[digamma(gamma_i)-digamma(sum_j gamma_j)] and gamma_i=alpha_i+sum_n phi_ni. Variational EM optimizes the evidence lower bound, updating B from expected topic-word counts and alpha numerically. Section 5.4 separately places Dirichlet priors on B; then the assignment update uses expected log topic probabilities, not fixed B values.

limitations: The base construction is a normalized distribution of indexed co-occurrences. It has no LDA-style population prior on new document mixtures; fold-in estimation is possible, so this is not a claim that unseen documents cannot be represented at all.

Training-document mixture parameters grow with the corpus. Maximum-likelihood or tempered fitting can overfit; local EM optimization, initialization and rank selection do not guarantee global optimality or unique factors. Permuting topic labels preserves the law, and linearly dependent topic distributions can yield nonunique mixture weights.

The bag-of-words representation omits token order and explicit within-topic word interactions. It is not a raw-count Poisson MRF, a canonical-parameter admixture, or a neural density estimator. Topic labels and selected high-probability words are interpretations, not verified semantic or causal categories.

Positive-count cells require positive modeled mass. Responsibility updates need nonzero denominators; unused components require a specified handling convention. Zero-count terms use the standard zero-contribution convention.

Historical retrieval experiments use particular corpora, ranks, held-out tempering and cosine interpolation. No universal retrieval advantage, exact new-document marginal likelihood or author implementation is certified.

claims.statement: For finite document indices d, vocabulary items w and K latent classes z, choose normalized nonnegative distributions pi_z, a_z(d) and b_z(w), and define p(d,w)=sum_z pi_z*a_z(d)*b_z(w). Given z, d and w are independent. Equivalently, for p(d)>0, p(w|d)=sum_z theta_dz*b_z(w), where theta_dz=pi_z*a_z(d)/p(d). Fit observed counts n(d,w) with sum_dw n(d,w)*log p(d,w). An exact EM E-step computes r_dwz=pi_z*a_z(d)*b_z(w)/p(d,w); M-steps normalize the corresponding count-weighted responsibilities over words, documents and classes. Each conditional document word distribution is an arithmetic convex combination of topic probabilities. In the original fold-in procedure, keep b_z(w) fixed and fit a new query or document’s mixture weights. This introduces new fitted weights rather than integrating over a population prior as in LDA.

native_neighbors.name: Sparse additive generative model
native_neighbors.definition: A generative model family for categorical text data that forms word probabilities by normalizing a background log-frequency vector plus sparse component deviations, allowing multiple generative facets to combine additively in log space.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: SAGE here denotes Eisenstein, Ahmed and Xing’s sparse additive generative construction, not Sage mathematical software or graph-neural aggregation. Its classification, topic and multifaceted uses share this parameterization; it is not synonymous with all naive Bayes models, sparse dictionary learning, sparse topic proportions or an arithmetic mixture of component word distributions. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 352 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; worktree returned 15 lines and main 19. All 16 unique matched contents were read: DocNADE contrasts, frontier and review references, plus four ignored-environment Sage/Pygments entries unrelated to AI SAGE. Twenty-one exact AIO nodes and four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Sparsity concerns log deviations. Finite logits still give positive word probabilities, and even zero-deviation words can change absolute probability through normalization; their relative odds remain those of the background when their deviations agree.

Additive log facets yield multiplicative unnormalized effects, not an arithmetic probability mixture. The model family does not require every document to have a single observed class or prohibit latent variables.

The Jeffreys-prior paragraph on PDF p.4 prints expected inverse variance equal to eta squared. Its preceding Gamma moment and b=eta squared/(a-1) instead give 1/eta squared for nonzero eta, with a>1 and positive scale. The printed final identity is not adopted; zero deviations require a limiting/numerical treatment. The improper prior is not represented as a normalized marginal distribution.

The paper warns that warm-starting tightly coupled deviation/variance updates can lock in early sparsity patterns. Neither approximate inference nor Newton updates establish global convergence or calibrated posterior uncertainty.

The single-component rank-one Hessian argument is not asserted unchanged for sums over multiple facet combinations. No author implementation, universal predictive advantage or numerical benchmark result is certified.

claims.statement: For a component k, set p(w=i|k) proportional to exp(m_i+eta_ki), normalizing over the vocabulary. Multiple selected facets contribute a sum of their deviation vectors before this normalization; no additional token-level switch is needed to choose which facet generates the word. This does not remove latent topic assignments used by a topic-model variant. The paper places sparsity-inducing priors on deviations, using zero-mean Gaussian components with latent variances: an exponential variance prior gives a Laplace marginal, while an alternative improper Jeffreys prior gives a different shrinkage construction. It combines MAP estimates of deviations with variational treatment of other latent quantities. For a single component and fixed expected precisions, the gradient is observed or expected counts minus total count times word probabilities minus the precision-weighted deviations; its Hessian is a rank-one term minus a diagonal term, enabling the reported efficient Newton update.

native_neighbors.name: Replicated Softmax
native_neighbors.definition: An undirected document model with binary hidden units and a length-dependent set of categorical word units that share visible-to-hidden weights, with hidden biases scaled by document length.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is the original Replicated Softmax model of Salakhutdinov and Hinton. It specializes a restricted Boltzmann machine to word-count sufficient statistics across documents of different lengths. It is distinct from repeatedly applying the ordinary softmax function, from the expected-count Constrained Poisson update discussed in the paper, and from the directed deterministic-feature Document NADE architecture. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 352 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; worktree returned 15 lines and main 19. All 16 unique matched contents were read: DocNADE contrasts, frontier and review references, plus four ignored-environment Sage/Pygments entries unrelated to AI SAGE. Twenty-one exact AIO nodes and four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Tractable hidden posteriors do not make the partition function or equilibrium model expectation tractable. Finite-step contrastive-divergence updates are not exact maximum-likelihood gradients; deterministic expected counts are not the same as multinomial Gibbs sampling.

The model is conditional on document length and supplies no document-length distribution. Its hidden feature vector has independent conditional Bernoulli coordinates, not topic proportions constrained to sum to one.

For ordinary counting measure on K^D ordered word assignments and F binary hidden units, the zero-weight, zero-bias partition is K^D times 2^F. The AIS discussion’s printed Z_0=2^F needs a corresponding normalized base-measure convention or visible-state factor; it is not adopted unchanged as that counting-measure partition. This is a mathematical qualification of the displayed derivation, not a claim about author-code behavior.
No convergence, topic quality or benchmark advantage is asserted. The later experimental pages and author software were not audited.

claims.statement: For a document with D word positions, vocabulary counts n_k and binary hidden states h_j, use energy E(V,h)=-sum_jk W_jk h_j n_k-sum_k b_k n_k-D sum_j a_j h_j. The joint probability is proportional to exp(-E) with a partition function for that length. Hidden units are conditionally independent given words, with P(h_j=1|V)=sigmoid(D a_j+sum_k W_jk n_k). Given h, positions independently draw words from softmax(b_k+sum_j W_jk h_j); equivalently, sample D word counts from the corresponding multinomial. Parameter sharing makes the ordered-word probability permutation invariant. A count-vector probability includes the number of distinct ordered realizations. Learning contrasts data and model sufficient statistics; the paper approximates the model term with finite alternating Gibbs steps initialized at data.

native_neighbors.name: Admixture of Poisson Markov random fields
native_neighbors.definition: A probabilistic topic-model family that draws each document from a proper Poisson-MRF base distribution whose canonical unary and interaction parameters are convex combinations of topic parameters under document-specific simplex weights.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: APM denotes the Poisson-MRF admixture construction in this source. It mixes parameters within one document-specific distribution, rather than choosing one topic for the entire document or summing independently drawn fixed-total topic vectors. Its narrow canonical-space form differs from LDA probability-space mixing and from the broader transformed-parameter admixture framework in the same paper. Shared words such as sparse, graphical or softmax do not identify it with SAGE, Replicated Softmax or a neural output layer. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels and all scoped synonyms and 415 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, yielding six and three matched lines; all five unique contents were read and describe existing frontier references, not records of these identities. The three-character APM acronym was checked in normalized identities but omitted from broad text search; the longer LPMRF acronym was included. Preparation included the three final GRM records before their merge; their inspected bytes are unchanged. All 188 semantic label/synonym hits were read. Fifty-one fully annotated exact CLASS nodes and outgoing edges were inspected: 46 byte-verified against prior reading and five fully read here. Seventy-eight full contextual YAMLs comprise 51 generated and 27 native records: six were fully read during this preparation and 72 byte-verified after prior full reading. Absence is bounded to the pinned snapshot, maintained corpus and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Topic components must share the same statistics, support and reference measure before averaging their natural parameters. Unrestricted positive raw-count Poisson interactions are not normalizable; positive-edge plots do not remove that restriction.

The original source describes modified sufficient statistics for positive interactions. The NIPS 2014 follow-up and public v0.9.1 release have now been inspected: the release instead fits raw-count asymmetric nodewise regressions without a sufficient-statistic transformation or joint admissibility constraints. This code does not certify the source-described proper positive-edge model. Other historical implementations and experimental runs are not inferred from this release.

The proposed prior’s claimed beta->beta+x posterior closure is not generally valid for its interaction coefficient: beta*beta^T+x*x^T differs from (beta+x)*(beta+x)^T. Its Gamma analogy also depends on the reference measure, gamma and the quadratic penalty. No exact conjugacy or calibrated posterior claim is adopted.

The displayed approximate-posterior expression is a sum of log-like terms despite being labeled as a posterior. Pseudolikelihood, l1 regularization and FISTA-like proximal updates are approximate fitting machinery; their availability does not make the jointly coupled topic/weight objective globally convex.

Canonical mixing generally differs from LDA arithmetic probability mixing. The 2015 fixed-length paper explicitly treats APM as an indirect relaxation and its summed-topic construction as a different model. Neither a single-document Poisson identity nor a coherence comparison proves equality of the full Bayesian models.

The preliminary 20 Newsgroup experiment used only 200 words and reported final APM fits with no interaction edges. Those coherence scores do not validate recovered dependency structure. Grolier graph illustrations were manually filtered and are qualitative, not causal or held-out performance evidence. No author code, fitting or benchmark was reproduced.

claims.statement: For k topics sharing a specified proper Poisson-MRF exponential-family base, sufficient statistics and count support, let topic natural parameters be (theta_j,Theta_j). Draw document weights w from Dirichlet(alpha), alpha_j>0, and form theta_bar=sum_j w_j*theta_j and Theta_bar=sum_j w_j*Theta_j. Draw x from the normalized base law at these averaged canonical parameters. The paper also proposes priors on topic parameters; this construction requires those priors to be proper on an admissible parameter domain. Convex combinations of finite natural parameters of the same exponential family remain in its finite-partition domain by Holder’s inequality. In the raw-count, unbounded, zero-diagonal PMRF case, symmetric off-diagonal interactions must be nonpositive. The paper states that its positive-interaction implementation instead uses modified sufficient statistics from Yang et al. 2013 while retaining abbreviated raw-PMRF notation. Those modifications must be specified consistently; averaging invalid positive raw-count parameters does not make them proper. In the raw-count Poisson case with all interactions zero, canonical mixing averages log rates and hence geometrically mixes rates. A modified sufficient statistic need not give an ordinary independent Poisson law. LDA mixes word probabilities arithmetically for the same weights; the Poisson-total/multinomial identity alone does not equate these document-weight parameterizations.

claims.statement: The NIPS 2014 follow-up relaxes symmetry to fit independent nodewise regression coefficients, alternating topic parameters with document simplex weights. Its Appendix C describes OR/AND edge selection and coefficient averaging as post-processing. In the inspected public v0.9.1 source, raw counts enter exponentiated linear predictors with zero self coefficients and unrestricted directed interaction estimates. Returned coefficient arrays are not constrained to be compatible conditionals of a normalized joint law. Neither averaging directed coefficients nor numerically capping rates supplies the modified-statistic base required for a proper positive-edge APM. This separates the probability-model definition from the released fitting surrogate; it does not identify that release with every experiment in either paper.

native_neighbors.name: Fixed-length Poisson MRF topic model
native_neighbors.definition: A probabilistic topic model that allocates a document total among topics, draws an independent fixed-length Poisson-MRF count vector for each allocated topic total, and sums those latent vectors to produce the observed document counts.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is the LPMRF topic hierarchy of Inouye et al. 2015, distinct from a single LPMRF, a mixture assigning one component per document, and an APM that averages topic canonical parameters before drawing a document. Conditional on topic allocations, its document law is a convolution of topic count distributions. Sparse additive categorical logits and latent binary Replicated Softmax architectures do not define this hierarchy. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels and all scoped synonyms and 415 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, yielding six and three matched lines; all five unique contents were read and describe existing frontier references, not records of these identities. The three-character APM acronym was checked in normalized identities but omitted from broad text search; the longer LPMRF acronym was included. Preparation included the three final GRM records before their merge; their inspected bytes are unchanged. All 188 semantic label/synonym hits were read. Fifty-one fully annotated exact CLASS nodes and outgoing edges were inspected: 46 byte-verified against prior reading and five fully read here. Seventy-eight full contextual YAMLs comprise 51 generated and 27 native records: six were fully read during this preparation and 72 byte-verified after prior full reading. Absence is bounded to the pinned snapshot, maintained corpus and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The hierarchy defines the model; the alternating hard/MAP allocation and surrogate-parameter updates are approximations. They do not by themselves guarantee exact posterior inference, marginal likelihood or monotone ascent of the true likelihood.

The displayed negative-log-posterior objective on p. 6 prints Pr rather than log Pr in its data term. Its topic-transfer expression adds a to the second total’s partition index even though that topic loses a counts; the required total is m_q-a. These displayed expressions are not copied as verified algorithms.

Zero topic allocations, the chosen length distribution and the per-topic normalization must be handled explicitly. The proposed prior evaluated at topic proportions does not automatically supply the exact posterior implied by the generative hierarchy.

Finite fixed-total support ensures normalization, but does not make partition computation or parameter estimation trivial. Adding a length distribution requires the correctly normalized conditional distribution at each total; one normalizer cannot be reused across lengths.

The source reuses nodewise Poisson regression from an unbounded model as a surrogate estimator. A fixed-total count coordinate is deterministic given all other count coordinates, so this is not its exact count-coordinate pseudolikelihood. Graph-recovery guarantees for a different Cartesian-support model do not automatically transfer.

For a general symmetric Phi, a token-label Gibbs update has log weight theta_s+2*(Phi*x_minus)_s+Phi_ss. The printed sampler omits Phi_ss and needs zero/equal diagonals or a specified reparameterization. The printed eigenvalue bound using L^2*lambda_max also needs lambda_max>=0; for arbitrary symmetric matrices a safe loose bound uses its nonnegative part. These are curator qualifications of displayed formulas, not reproduced code defects.

The length-dependent interaction weighting and curve fitted above AIS estimates are modeling and numerical choices. A curve above finitely many estimated log partitions is not a certified upper bound on every exact partition value. No AIS convergence, likelihood accuracy or author implementation was validated.

The reported topic-model perplexities use MAP latent assignments, as the source explicitly notes, rather than exact marginalization over all topic allocations. Qualitative word pairs and historical timing curves do not establish causal relations, generic superiority or current performance. No author fit or benchmark was reproduced.

claims.statement: With fixed topic parameters (theta_j,Phi_j), draw document weights w from Dirichlet(alpha) with positive alpha, a total L from the chosen length law (Poisson in the stated example), and topic totals m from Multinomial(L,w). Conditional on m, draw z_j independently from LPMRF(theta_j,Phi_j,total=m_j) and set x=sum_j z_j. Each z_j uses its own finite-total partition function; topic parameters may include the explicitly chosen length-dependent weighting. At m_j=0 the topic vector is zero. Given w and L, the document mass sums products of these normalized topic masses over compatible z allocations and weights each m allocation by its Multinomial(L,w) probability. It is not a single LPMRF evaluated at averaged canonical parameters. With every Phi_j=0, z_j is multinomial with probabilities softmax(theta_j), and the allocation hierarchy gives the familiar LDA conditional token construction for fixed topic probabilities. That reduction does not assert equality of arbitrary priors on the topic parameters or equivalence of the paper’s approximate fitting procedure to exact LDA inference.

native_neighbors.name: Structured variational inference for factorial HMMs
native_neighbors.definition: A variational inference procedure for factorial hidden Markov models that approximates the posterior by independent chain-path distributions while retaining temporal dependence within each chain.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes the chain-structured approximation and additive-Gaussian updates in Ghahramani–Jordan Section 3.5 and Appendix D. It is narrower than all structured variational inference and distinct from the factorial HMM model, a fully factorized state-by-time approximation, exact joint-state forward–backward, Gibbs sampling, or BBVI score-function optimization. It requires neither an amortized recognition network nor a variational autoencoder architecture. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 376 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines. All 4 unique matched contents were fully read: preceding boundary discussions, citations, reviews and pending leads, not existing records of these three identities. All 64 semantic label/synonym hits, 17 exact fully annotated AIO nodes with outgoing edges, their generated records and four native neighbors were inspected or verified unchanged after prior full reading. Absence is bounded to this pin and inspected neighborhood.
limitations: The approximation removes posterior dependence between chains even when the shared observation creates explaining-away effects. It preserves each chain’s time dependence, unlike a fully factorized state-by-time distribution.

The h factors are positive unnormalized potentials, not row-normalized transition probabilities or already-normalized state posteriors. Normalization and initial/boundary conditions belong to the complete chain computation.

The residual/diagonal formula depends on additive Gaussian emissions with common covariance. General emissions require their own expected-log-factor calculations; the formula is not an arbitrary-model black-box update.

Coordinate-ascent guarantees require an exact update of one factor while holding the others fixed. Simultaneous arbitrary updates, local stopping criteria or approximate model steps do not establish a global optimum, exact evidence, or universal likelihood improvement.

Appendix C Equation C.9 displays prior/transition signs inconsistent with its energy definition and derivative; that display is not adopted. Appendix D cancels explicit prior/transition log terms when the same factors are retained, but its moments and normalizer still depend on those factors; the accompanying independence wording is not literal total independence.

The general product-of-path-distributions variational family contains independent-time factors, but the displayed fixed-transition/unary parameterization and local optimization do not justify claiming every run outperforms a fully factorized approximation. No benchmark or author implementation is certified.

claims.statement: For fixed model parameters and observations, choose q(S)=product_m q_m(s_1:T^m) and optimize the evidence lower bound E_q[log p(Y,S)-log q(S)], equivalently minimizing KL(q||p(S|Y)). Each chain factor is globally normalized over its path and retains the model’s initial and transition factors multiplied by positive unary potentials h_t^m. In the additive Gaussian model, h_t^m is proportional to exp((W_m)^T C^-1 [y_t-sum_(l!=m) W_l E_q[s_t^l]] - 0.5 diag((W_m)^T C^-1 W_m)), componentwise over the chain’s states. With other chain factors fixed, run forward–backward using these unary factors to update that chain’s state and temporal-pair moments, then repeat across chains. Same-time moments between different chains factorize under q; within-chain temporal moments do not. Such exact single-chain coordinate updates increase or preserve the bound for fixed model parameters. The moments may also supply a variational E-step for model fitting, but this approximate posterior does not become the exact posterior merely by convergence.

native_neighbors.name: Black box variational inference
native_neighbors.definition: A variational-inference procedure that estimates evidence-lower-bound gradients from samples of a tractable variational distribution using its score function and model log joint, with mean-field local signals and score control variates to manage estimator variance.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record covers Ranganath, Gerrish and Blei’s original BBVI Algorithms 1–2 and their score-function estimator, mean-field local signals and control variates. It is not every black-box inference method, a pathwise reparameterization estimator, a model architecture or an amortized recognition network such as NVIL. The hierarchical data-subsampling extension is outside the validated mechanism scope here. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 337 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 22 and 22 lines respectively. All 15 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: the preceding gradient-estimator records, their cited Bengio source, saved source-reading scopes, reviews and open discovery leads, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Thirteen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Black box still requires sampling from and evaluating the variational distribution, score derivatives with respect to its parameters, and evaluation of the model log joint at sampled latent states. The method does not require differentiation through a discrete latent sample, but support and integrability conditions remain necessary.

Raw unbiasedness requires the regularity assumptions behind differentiation under the expectation and zero expected score. A model normalization constant independent of lambda cancels from this gradient; a parameter-dependent term cannot be discarded on that basis.

A coefficient fixed independently of the gradient samples preserves expectation when the relevant moments exist. A coefficient estimated from those same samples can correlate with the sample score and introduce bias. The paper reports separate sample counts for coefficient estimation and gradient calculation, but the inspected description does not establish an exact sampling-independence convention; no implementation behavior is asserted.

Population-optimal control-variate scaling and conditional-expectation variance reduction do not guarantee that estimated coefficients or every additional removal of zero-mean terms reduces finite-sample variance. Zero or poorly estimated score variance requires handling beyond division by the displayed ratio.

The practical step schedule and change-in-parameters stopping rule do not establish global optimality or exact posterior recovery. Mean-field factorization can limit the approximation. The printed hierarchical subsampling formulas need a separate weighting audit and are not curated as a verified extension here.
No benchmark result, author-code run, general convergence proof or posterior-quality certification is included.

claims.statement: For fixed observed x and joint model p(x,z), choose a variational family q(z;lambda), sample z from q, and maximize L(lambda)=E_q[log p(x,z)-log q(z;lambda)] by stochastic ascent. Under the normalized-score and differentiation-under-expectation conditions, the raw gradient is E_q[grad_lambda log q(z;lambda)*(log p(x,z)-log q(z;lambda))], estimated by a Monte Carlo average. The mean-field version factors q into q_i(z_i;lambda_i) and uses for each factor the model log terms that depend on z_i together with -log q_i; unrelated terms cancel in expectation under the stated factorization. For parameter coordinate d in factor i, let h_d be the score and f_d be that score times the local log signal. A fixed control-variate coefficient gives f_d-a_d*h_d because E[h_d]=0; the population variance-minimizing coefficient is Cov(f_d,h_d)/Var(h_d) when these quantities exist and Var(h_d)>0. The source estimates coefficients from samples and averages corrected contributions before a stochastic-ascent update. Its fixed-coefficient expectation identity does not by itself justify arbitrary reuse of samples to estimate both the coefficient and corrected gradient.

native_neighbors.name: Bayesian Data Augmentation for Deep Models
native_neighbors.definition: Tran et al.’s supervised deep-learning procedure that treats synthetic labeled examples as latent data, repeatedly samples them from an evolving learned model and updates model parameters through a generalized Monte Carlo expectation-maximization formulation.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record is scoped to the 2017 Tran et al. formulation for generating labeled deep-learning training examples. It is not all statistical Bayesian data augmentation, generic EM, Bayesian-network graphical modeling or posterior sampling of neural-network weights. Its class-conditioned generative model differs from AdaMixUp’s interpolation and cooperative intrusion discriminator. Generalized Monte Carlo EM is the formulation used here, not an alias identifying every GMCEM application with this record. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 250 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main checkout, returning 9 lines in each checkout. These were references within neighboring records, their review and the prior discovery ledger, not records for the proposed identities. Fourteen exact AIO CLASS nodes with synonyms and outgoing edges and six neighboring native mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The generalized M-step requires improvement of its objective. Differentiability alone does not guarantee that an arbitrary finite gradient step or a noisy minibatch epoch increases that objective.

The source’s Lemma 1 moves from a sampled-objective inequality to an expectation inequality. Improvement observed for one finite sample does not by itself guarantee improvement of the exact expected objective or the observed-data posterior, especially when the update is selected using that sample. No unconditional monotonicity or convergence guarantee for practical GAN training is asserted.

Equations (18)–(19) link authenticator losses to data log-likelihood terms. A real/fake discriminator probability is not itself a normalized data density; this record describes the published adversarial surrogate without asserting an exact normalized-likelihood or exact-EM implementation.

Separate real and synthetic means assign each group its own normalization. Increasing the number of generated samples does not automatically multiply the synthetic group’s total coefficient in the printed objective.
Generated labels and images depend on the fitted model and optimization. No label-correctness guarantee, universal sample quality, benchmark advantage or reproduction of author software is asserted.

claims.statement: Treat each additional labeled example z=(t_a,x_a) as a latent variable and seek a maximum-a-posteriori parameter estimate, rather than sampling a posterior over all network weights. At an iteration, sample synthetic labeled data using the current model and approximate the expected augmented log posterior with a Monte Carlo average. The generalized M-step seeks parameters that increase this sampled objective rather than solving a global maximization exactly. The published objective includes a parameter prior, an average of real-data label/data log terms and a separate average of synthetic-data label/data log terms. In the paper’s concrete GAN realization, a class-conditioned generator produces labeled images, a classifier learns dataset labels on real and generated examples, and a separate authenticator distinguishes real from generated images. The published discriminative step minimizes J_C+J_AG, while the generative step minimizes J_C−J_AG, combining class consistency with adversarial realism. J_C separately averages the real and synthetic classification losses, rather than averaging one pooled batch with weights determined solely by its real-to-synthetic count ratio. The practical training procedure uses minibatches and one epoch of stochastic updates per parameter-update iteration. The GAN architecture is one realization of the augmentation framework, not a requirement for every possible realization.
